The grid services objectives of the program were to effectively integrate intermittent renewable resources, enhance resiliency and outage response at the distribution level, ensure resource adequacy particularly during periods of disruptive events, and defer capital expenses for distribution infrastructure upgrades that serve the community of buildings. The objectives were to be accomplished by completing tasks in six focus areas, see Figure 1. The first area was grid services that focused Figure 1. Project Focus Area on the utility interaction with DERs. PacifiCorp worked directly with technology partners to develop models and tools to incorporate DERs into the electrical grid. The second area focused on the consumer side of the DERs like efficiency targets and consumer experiences which ensures recruitment and retention. PacifiCorp worked with partners to design efficiency measures and survey occupant experiences to ensure the project is on track. The third area focused on cybersecurity, privacy, and technical standards. PacifiCorp worked with partner experts to develop a robust Cybersecurity plan. The fourth area was to develop business models for integrating DERs into wholesale delivery markets and long-term utility resource planning. The fifth area evaluated how the UDERMS project can be replicated and applied across the country. Lastly, the sixth ensured that data is collected and shared with the National Coordinator. 5.1 Original Hypotheses The project hypothesis was to demonstrate a combined 8.26 megawatts (MW) of flexible loads from the participating buildings to be used for frequency support, demand response and other applicable grid services. The EE objectives were to show that significant savings of at least 30% could be realized through design changes to new buildings and operational improvements for existing buildings. Once the flexible loads and efficient savings were demonstrated the plan was to develop viable business models that can be replicated across the country. The team identified a diverse but representative set of buildings to include in the pilot project. The buildings range from a large suburban apartment complex, downtown complex of mixed-use retail and apartments, University laboratory and office building with a microgrid, a mass transit transportation center, manufacturing building, and residential home. The buildings are all-electric and will have advanced energy efficiency technologies with efficient heat pump-based HVAC (both central and mini-splits) and domestic hot water, adaptive building envelope, and advanced lighting achieving a minimum of 30% energy efficiency compared to the baseline of typical buildings. Each building contains multiple DERs with flexible loads, including renewable energy either onsite or part of a community solar farm, battery storage, and electric vehicle charging equipment.
